learning_outcomes.text: Analyze an existing system and improve it.
Distinguish between reality and the models used to describe or modify it.
Understand the notion of uncertainty in the management of the project, in its realization, and in the results obtained.

Develop all aspects of a business project according to a lean or agile methodology, including: developing a business model based on an identified need in a target audience and a technical solution to meet that need.
Conduct a quantitative and qualitative market study through documentary research, interviews, and online surveys.
Confront the project with the reactions of various stakeholders: potential customers, commercial or industrial partners.
Iteratively improve the project based on feedback and information obtained.
Establish a credible financial plan to enable the development of the company and determine the financing needs.
Establish and test a prototype or develop a convincing technical plan to establish the feasibility of the project.
Prepare and practice a start-up project pitch for potential customers or investors.

syllabus_topics: Difference between startups and large companies
Startup project validation in a co-creation approach
teaching_methods: Group work on the development of an actual business project
Regular interactions with an experienced coach, including through presentations
Learning of the 'lean startup' methodology for creating a business through group discussions of videocasts
Confrontation of ideas and assumptions with the real world through discussions with potential customers and commercial or industrial partners
Development and testing of a prototype with stakeholders

assessment_methods.method: Project grade (realization, written presentations, oral presentations/interactions, organization of work, reflective posture, mastery of concepts)

assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of a project grade (group and individualized) and an individual written test grade. The individual written test's weight in the final grade is 25% if successful, but increases in case of failure: it is 100% for a grade <= 6, and evolves linearly between 6 and 10 according to the formula: weight = 1 - 0.75 * (grade - 6)/4. The project grade part cannot be redone in the second session. The second session will consist of an individual exam, possibly requiring prior individual work.
degree: Bachelor in Engineering (Bachelier en sciences de l'ingénieur, orientation ingénieur civil) - FSA1BA
